newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Convicts riot in Bogota jail.
newsitem.headline: Convicts riot in Bogota jail.

text.p: More than 2,000 prisoners including convicted leftist guerrillas rioted and started fires in Bogota's La Modelo jail early on Tuesday to protest over cramped conditions, prison authorities said.
About 800 prison officers and police fired tear gas at the rioters and and restored relative calm to the jail, according to a spokesman for the National Prisons' Institute (INPEC).

The riot flared in two prison wings shortly after midnight when guards confiscated liquor from a group of inmates. There were no reports of injuries, INPEC officer Col. Hugo Alfonso Cepeda told reporters.

A Reuters photographer outside the jail reported palls of smoke hanging over the prison and said hundreds of masked prisoners had climbed onto the jail roof, brandishing sticks and clubs and makeshift signs. One of the signs read "End prison overcrowding," another said "ELN present," a reference to the National Liberation Army (ELN) rebel force, some of whose members are among the rioting convicts.

An INPEC spokesman said at least 2,100 prisoners were housed in the two wings, which are designed for just 1,200 convicts. He said all the prisoners joined an initially small group of rioters but stressed the problems had not spilled over to the high security wing, home to convicted henchmen of the late druglord Pablo Escobar, notorious head of the Medellin drug cartel.

"There is overcrowding in these wings. We have never tried to hide that fact. At the moment it is worse because we are remodeling some of the facilities," the spokesman said. "One of the wings contains convicted guerrillas but these are not rebel chieftains," he added.
At least two fires were started in a carpentry and shoe repair workshop but the spokesman said firefighters had extinguished the blazes.

Representatives of the public prosecutor's office, the Human Rights Ombudsman and the International Committee of the Red Cross went to talk to the inmates and the prison spokesman said the situation was "calm" and added: "There is nothing to suggest this will flare up again."
